name: Chess
shortDescription: The world's most popular strategy game: checkmate the enemy king to win.
rules:
8 × 8 board, White moves first. The **king** moves one square any way. The **queen** moves any distance straight or diagonally. The **rook** moves straight and the **bishop** diagonally, any distance. The **knight** moves in an L and jumps over pieces. A **pawn** moves one square forward (two on its first move) and captures one square diagonally.

**Castling:** the king moves two squares towards a rook, and the rook jumps to its other side. Only if neither has moved, the squares between are empty, the king is not in check and does not pass through an attacked square.

**En passant:** a pawn that has just moved two squares past an enemy pawn can be captured as if it had moved one, but only on the very next move.

**Promotion:** a pawn reaching the last rank becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight.

You may not leave your king in check. A side that is **checkmated** loses. It is a draw when the side to move is not in check but has no move (stalemate), the same position occurs three times, 50 moves each pass without a pawn move or capture, or neither side has enough material to mate.

learn.title: Learn chess
learn.subtitle: Meet each piece and a few famous openings, one step at a time.
learn.found: Found {n} of {total} squares this piece can reach. Tap those squares!
learn.tryDone: Great job! You know how it moves.
learn.tryWrong: Not quite, this piece can't go there. Look at the dots again.
learn.challengeStart: Tap the white piece, then tap square {square} (the one with the gold ring).
learn.challengeNotGoal: That move is allowed, but it's not the gold ring. Try again!
learn.challengeIllegal: This piece can't go there. Tap the white piece to see where it can go.
learn.yourTurn: Your turn. Find the move that fits the idea above.
learn.wrongMove: That's not the move in this lesson. Try again or tap Hint.

pawn.meet: The pawn is the smallest piece. Each side has 8. Pawns only go forward, never backward.
pawn.move: A pawn moves one square straight ahead. On its very first move it may jump two squares.
pawn.try: Tap the squares the pawn can move to.
pawn.challenge: A pawn captures diagonally forward, not straight. Capture the black pawn with the white one.
pawn.fun: A pawn that reaches the far end of the board turns into a stronger piece, usually a queen!

rook.meet: The rook looks like a castle tower. It is very strong when the path is open.
rook.move: A rook moves in straight lines, along rows or columns, any number of squares, but it cannot jump over pieces.
rook.try: Tap the squares the rook can move to.
rook.challenge: A rook captures by moving onto an enemy piece. Capture the black pawn.
rook.fun: Two rooks working together are a fearsome team.

bishop.meet: The bishop wears a pointed hat and always moves diagonally.
bishop.move: A bishop moves along diagonals, any number of squares. It always stays on the same square colour.
bishop.try: Tap the squares the bishop can move to.
bishop.challenge: Use the diagonal to capture the far-away black pawn.
bishop.fun: Each side has two bishops: one on light squares, one on dark squares.

knight.meet: The knight looks like a horse. It is the only piece that can jump over others.
knight.move: A knight moves in an L: two squares one way, then one square sideways. It can jump over pieces.
knight.try: Tap the squares the knight can jump to.
knight.challenge: Jump in an L to capture the black pawn.
knight.fun: Knights are great when the board is crowded.

queen.meet: The queen is the strongest piece on the board.
queen.move: A queen moves like a rook and a bishop together: straight or diagonal, any number of squares.
queen.try: Tap the squares the queen can move to.
queen.challenge: Use the queen's path to capture the black pawn.
queen.fun: The queen is powerful, so be careful not to lose her too early.

king.meet: The king is the most important piece. Lose the king and you lose the game!
king.move: A king moves one square in any direction. It may never step onto a square the enemy attacks.
king.try: Tap the squares the king can move to.
king.challenge: A king can capture too, if nobody protects the piece. Capture the black pawn.
king.fun: Protect your king carefully. Checkmating the enemy king is how you win.

italian.name: Italian Game
italian.intro: A classic, easy-to-understand opening: take the centre and aim the bishop at the weak point of the enemy.
italian.s0: The king pawn goes two squares (e4). It takes the centre and opens lines for the bishop and queen.
italian.s1: Black also pushes the king pawn two squares to fight for the centre.
italian.s2: The knight comes to f3: it attacks the e5 pawn and develops a piece.
italian.s3: The black knight comes to c6 to protect the e5 pawn.
italian.s4: The bishop goes to c4, the move that gives the Italian Game its name. It eyes f7, Black's weak spot.
italian.s5: Black also develops a bishop, to c5.
italian.s6: The c3 pawn prepares d4 to take even more of the centre.
italian.s7: The black knight comes to f6: it develops and attacks the e4 pawn.
italian.s8: The d4 pawn attacks the black bishop and takes the centre.
italian.s10: White captures back with the c3 pawn. White has a big centre and well-placed pieces.
italian.sum1: Bring out knights and bishops early.
italian.sum2: The bishop on c4 eyes the weak f7 square.

queens-gambit.name: Queen's Gambit
queens-gambit.intro: White starts with the queen pawn and offers a pawn, which White can usually win back.
queens-gambit.s0: The queen pawn goes two squares (d4): a solid way to take the centre.
queens-gambit.s1: Black answers with the queen pawn to block the centre.
queens-gambit.s2: The c4 pawn attacks d5. This is the "gambit": White is happy to trade a pawn for the centre.
queens-gambit.s3: Black protects the d5 pawn with e6.
queens-gambit.s4: The knight on c3 develops and pressures d5.
queens-gambit.s5: The black knight comes to f6 to develop and protect d5.
queens-gambit.s6: The bishop to g5 pins the f6 knight and annoys Black.
queens-gambit.s7: The black bishop to e7 breaks the pin and prepares to castle.
queens-gambit.s8: The e3 pawn opens a path for the bishop and guards the centre.
queens-gambit.s9: Black castles to put the king in a safe place.
queens-gambit.s10: The knight from g1 comes to f3. Every white piece is now in the game.
queens-gambit.sum0: Take the centre with the queen pawn.
queens-gambit.sum2: Get ready to castle so the king is safe.

sicilian.name: Sicilian Defence
sicilian.intro: You play Black. This opening lets Black fight back by trading a side pawn for the white centre pawn.
sicilian.s0: White opens with the king pawn, e4.
sicilian.s1: The c5 pawn is the Sicilian move: Black controls d4 without copying White.
sicilian.s2: White brings the knight to f3, ready for d4.
sicilian.s3: The d6 pawn opens the black bishop and protects the centre.
sicilian.s4: White pushes d4 to open the centre.
sicilian.s5: Black captures on d4: a side pawn is traded for White's centre pawn.
sicilian.s6: White captures back with the knight.
sicilian.s7: The knight to f6 attacks the e4 pawn and develops a piece.
sicilian.s8: White plays the knight to c3 to protect e4.
sicilian.s9: The a6 pawn prepares Black to expand on the queenside.
sicilian.sum0: Black trades a side pawn (c) for White's centre pawn (d).
sicilian.sum1: Develop the knight early to attack e4.
sicilian.sum2: The queenside is where Black looks for counterplay.

ruy-lopez.name: Ruy Lopez
ruy-lopez.intro: A very famous opening, hundreds of years old. The white bishop puts pressure on the knight that protects the e5 pawn.
ruy-lopez.s0: The king pawn goes two squares (e4) to take the centre and open lines for the bishop and queen.
ruy-lopez.s1: Black also pushes the king pawn two squares to fight for the centre.
ruy-lopez.s2: The knight comes to f3: it attacks the e5 pawn and develops a piece.
ruy-lopez.s3: The black knight comes to c6 to protect the e5 pawn.
ruy-lopez.s4: The bishop goes to b5: the Ruy Lopez move. It eyes the c6 knight, which protects e5.
ruy-lopez.s5: Black pushes the a6 pawn to ask the bishop: "What are you going to do?"
ruy-lopez.s6: The bishop steps back to a4, still pressuring the c6 knight and safe from the pawn.
ruy-lopez.s7: The black knight comes to f6: it develops and attacks the e4 pawn.
ruy-lopez.s8: White castles: the king goes to safety and the rook comes towards the middle.
ruy-lopez.s9: The black bishop to e7 prepares to castle.
ruy-lopez.sum0: The bishop on b5 pressures the c6 knight.
ruy-lopez.sum1: Castle early to keep the king safe.

french.name: French Defence
french.intro: You play Black. This opening gives Black a solid position: the e6 and d5 pawns form a wall in front of the king.
french.s0: White opens with the king pawn, e4.
french.s1: The e6 pawn is the French move. It prepares d5 and opens a path for the bishop.
french.s2: White pushes d4 to take the centre.
french.s3: The d5 pawn attacks the e4 pawn and claims part of the centre for Black.
french.s4: The white knight comes to c3 to protect the e4 pawn.
french.s5: The black knight comes to f6: it develops and also eyes the e4 pawn.
french.s6: The white bishop goes to g5 and pins the f6 knight.
french.s7: The black bishop to e7 breaks the pin and prepares to castle.
french.s8: The e5 pawn attacks the f6 knight and gains space.
french.s9: The knight steps back to d7: it escapes the attack and keeps Black solid.
french.sum0: The e6 and d5 pawns make a solid position.
french.sum1: When a piece is pinned or attacked, find it a safe square.
french.sum2: Black waits for chances to strike at the centre later.

london.name: London System
london.intro: An easy opening to remember: White plays almost the same moves in many games.
london.s0: The queen pawn goes two squares (d4) to take the centre.
london.s1: Black answers with the queen pawn to block the centre.
london.s2: The bishop goes to f4 before the e3 pawn move, so the pawn does not block it. This is the London move.
london.s3: The black knight comes to f6 and develops.
london.s4: The e3 pawn protects the f4 bishop and opens a path for the other bishop.
london.s5: The e6 pawn gives Black a solid position.
london.s6: The knight from g1 comes to f3: it develops and controls the centre.
london.s7: The c5 pawn attacks White's d4 pawn.
london.s8: The c3 pawn protects d4 and holds the centre.
london.s9: The black knight comes to c6 to attack the d4 pawn.
london.sum0: Bring out the bishop before pushing e3.
london.sum1: The c3 and e3 pawns protect the d4 pawn.
london.sum2: The same set-up works in many games.

castling.name: Castling
castling.meet: Castling is the only move that moves two pieces at once: the king and a rook. It puts the king in safety.
castling.move: The king goes two squares towards the rook, and the rook jumps to the other side of the king. Watch White castle to the right.
castling.try: Now try castling to the left: tap the white king, then tap c1 (the square with the gold ring).
castling.fun: You can only castle if that king and rook have never moved, nothing is between them, and the king is not in check or crossing a square the enemy attacks.

en-passant.name: En passant
en-passant.meet: A special way to capture that many beginners do not know yet. It only happens with pawns.
en-passant.move: The black pawn jumps two squares and lands next to the white pawn. The white pawn may capture it as if it had moved just one square, and lands behind it.
en-passant.try: The black pawn just jumped two squares to d5, next to the white pawn. Tap the white pawn, then tap d6 to capture en passant.
en-passant.fun: You can only do it right away, on the very next move. If you play something else, the chance is gone.

promotion.name: Promotion
promotion.meet: A pawn that walks all the way to the far end of the board gets promoted. That is why even a small pawn matters.
promotion.move: When a pawn reaches the last row, it turns into a queen, rook, bishop or knight, as you choose. Watch the white pawn become a queen.
promotion.try: Tap the white pawn, then tap e8. Then choose the piece you want the pawn to become.
promotion.fun: Most players choose the queen because she is the strongest. You can have several queens at once!

coordinates.name: Meet the board: coordinates
coordinates.meet: The board is like a cinema and every square is a seat. The rows are numbered 1 to 8 (orange). The columns have letters a to h (blue). Seat e4 is in row 4, column e. The orange and blue lines cross at exactly that seat.

intro.rank: Rows have numbers. 1 is at the bottom, 8 at the top. Tap the row you hear.
intro.file: Columns have letters. a is on the left, h on the right. Tap the column you hear.
intro.cross: The seat you hear is where the orange and blue lines cross. Tap that seat.
intro.find: This time there are no lines. Find the seat yourself. Tap Hint if you need help.
intro.treasure: There is a treasure on the board. Choose the right name for its square.

prompt.treasure: Which square is the treasure on?

wrong.rank: Not quite. Rows are numbers, counted from the bottom: row 1 is at the bottom.
wrong.file: Not quite. Columns are letters, from left to right: a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h.
wrong.cross: Not quite. Look for where the orange and blue lines cross.
wrong.find: Not quite. Find the row number first, then the column letter. Tap Hint if you need it.
wrong.treasure: Not quite. Look at which row and which column the treasure is in.

coordinates.allDone: Great job! You finished this part.
coordinates.done: You can read the names of the squares on the board!
coordinates.fun: Now you can read moves like "Knight to f3". Try finding f3 on the board.

checkmate.name: Catch the king: check and checkmate
checkmate.meet: The king is shy! When a piece threatens to catch the king, we say "Check!" and the king must be saved right away. If there is no way to save the king, it is "Checkmate!" and the game is over. The king is never captured, but being checkmated means losing.

intro.check: The white king is under threat, shown by a red circle. Find the black piece that threatens the king.
intro.escape: When the king is in check there are three ways to save it: run (the king moves away), block (put a piece in between) or capture (take the piece that is attacking).
intro.judge: The king is in check. Look whether it can still be saved. If there is no way, that is checkmate.
intro.mate: Now you play White. Find the move that leaves the black king with no escape: checkmate!

prompt.check: Which piece is attacking the king? Tap that piece.

escape.run: Save the king by RUNNING: tap the king, then a safe square.
escape.block: Save the king by BLOCKING: put a piece between the attacker and the king.
escape.capture: Save the king by CAPTURING: take the piece that attacks the king.

prompt.judge: Can the white king still be saved?
prompt.mate: Find the checkmate. The black king has nowhere to go.

checkmate.allDone: Great job! You finished this part.

wrong.check: That piece does not attack the king. Find the piece aiming straight at it.

escape.illegal: That does not save the king. Tap one of your pieces, then a square with a dot.
escape.other: You saved the king by {did}, but this question asks for {asked}. Try again.

judge.rightSave: Correct! The king can be saved: run, block or capture.
judge.rightMate: Correct! No way to save the king. That is checkmate!
judge.wrong: Not quite. See if the king can run, block or capture.

mate.right: Checkmate! The black king has no escape. You win!
mate.escaped: The black king escaped! Try another move.
mate.stalemate: Oh, the black king cannot move but is not in check: a draw! Try another move.
mate.hint1: Hint: tap the piece on square {from}.
mate.hint2: Hint: tap the piece on {from}, then move it to {to}.
mate.noCheck: That move does not check the black king. Try another move.
mate.defended: Black found a way to save the king (block or capture)! Try another move.

checkmate.done: You know how to save the king and catch the king!
checkmate.fun: When you give checkmate, say it out loud: "Checkmate!". You won the game.

capture.name: Capturing and protecting
capture.meet: When your piece moves onto a square with an enemy piece, you "capture" it and it leaves the board. But the enemy can capture your pieces too! You need to know which of your pieces is in danger and which one is protected.

intro.take: Capture a black piece. Tap a white piece, then the black piece it can take. A circle around a black piece means it can be taken.
intro.attacked: This time Black moves. Find the white piece in danger: some black piece can take it.
intro.safe: The white piece can take a black piece. But look: does anything protect that black piece? If so, you will be taken back.
intro.value: Each piece is worth a different amount: pawn 1, knight and bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9. Trading a big piece for a small one is a loss.

prompt.attacked: Which white piece is in danger?
prompt.safe: The white piece can take this black piece. Should it?

take.notCapture: That is just a move, not a capture. Choose a move that takes a black piece.
take.hint: Hint: the highlighted black pieces can be taken.

attacked.wrong: That piece is safe. Find the white piece that a black piece can take.
attacked.right: Correct! The highlighted black piece can take that white piece.
attacked.hint: Hint: the highlighted black piece is aiming at a white piece.

safe.rightFree: Correct! Nothing protects that black piece, so it is free to take.
safe.rightGuarded: Correct! That black piece is protected (the highlighted piece takes back). You would lose your piece.
safe.wrongFree: Not quite. Nothing protects that black piece, so taking it is safe.
safe.wrongGuarded: Not quite. A black piece protects it: you would be taken back.

value.right: Correct! The {big} is worth {bigPoints} points, more than the {small} ({smallPoints} points).
value.wrong: Not quite. Remember: pawn 1, knight and bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9.

capture.allDone: Great job! You finished this part.
capture.done: You can capture pieces and you know which pieces need protecting!
capture.fun: From now on, before you capture, ask: does anything protect that piece?

tactics.name: Little tricks and endgames
tactics.meet: Chess has some great little tricks. A fork: one piece attacks two pieces at once, and the enemy can save only one. A pin: a piece in front of the king cannot move, or the king would be attacked. Two rooks working together can checkmate the king. And you need to know when a game is a draw.

intro.fork: Find the move that makes one of your pieces attack two big enemy pieces at once. The enemy can save only one, and you take the other!
intro.pin: A pinned piece stands right in front of the king: if it moves away, the king is attacked. Find the pinned white piece.
intro.mate: Two rooks work like a staircase: one rook cuts off the rows, the other gives check. Find the checkmate.
intro.draw: It is Black to move. Look: is the black king in check? Does Black have any move? That tells you if it is checkmate, a draw, or not over yet.

prompt.mate: Find the checkmate with two rooks.
prompt.draw: What is the state of the game?

fork.notFork: That move is not a fork. Find a move where one piece attacks two big pieces at once.
fork.right: A fork! The enemy can save only one piece.
fork.hint: Hint: tap the highlighted piece, then look for the square where it forks.

pin.right: Correct! This piece is pinned: if it moves away, the white king is attacked. The highlighted black piece is pinning it.
pin.wrong: Not quite. Find the white piece standing between the king and a black piece aiming at the king.
pin.hint: Hint: the highlighted black piece is aiming straight at the white king.

mate.right: Checkmate! The black king has no escape. You win!
mate.escaped: The black king escaped! Try another move.
mate.stalemate: Oh, the black king cannot move but is not in check: a draw! Try another move.
mate.noCheck: That move does not check the black king. Try another move.
mate.defended: Black found a way to save the king (block or capture)! Try another move.
mate.hint1: Hint: tap the piece on square {from}.
mate.hint2: Hint: tap the piece on {from}, then move it to {to}.

right.mate: Correct! The black king is in check and has no escape: checkmate.
right.stalemate: Correct! The black king is not in check but has no move at all: a draw. When you are winning, do not trap the king like that!
right.ongoing: Correct! Black still has moves, the game is not over.

draw.wrong: Not quite. Ask two questions: is the black king in check? Does Black have any move?

tactics.allDone: Great job! You finished this part.
tactics.done: You know forks, pinned pieces, two-rook mates and draws!
tactics.fun: Remember: before you move, look for a fork. And do not trap the enemy king without giving check.
